Feelings and instincts are just tools the early human brain acquired. They help make decisions and encourage favorable behavior for survival: your past negative experiences may coalesce into a bad feeling about traveling through a certain hazardous area, for example, so you instinctively avoid it without having to logically reasoning out why every time.

So when someone says "follow your heart" or "don't think, just do", they're telling you to leave your brain on autopilot and follow those feelings.

But why would anyone intentionally do that?

Easy: thinking is hard. Its literally energy intensive. Logically reasoning things out takes precious time, and there's no way you can conciously recall and step through every relevant memory either. Feelings are a rough sum of all those experiences (as well as inclinations hardwired into your brain with genes). So, in a way, your "heart" can be wiser than your logical mind will ever be.

Feelings are emotions, love, hate, jealousy, despair, ambition, vanity, self loathing, joy, sadness, anger, rage, sexual desire, discomfort, satiation, and so on.
